ai.description: *Leptobrachella nokrekensis* is a small toad (SVL 24–27 mm) with a brown dorsum featuring dark spots. It is distinguished by a granular skin texture, distinct toe discs, and a pale, unspotted venter.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Leptobrachella nokrekensis* is best distinguished by the presence of distinct, prominent, and rounded tubercles on its dorsal surface, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Leptobrachella nokrekensis* inhabits the primary subtropical evergreen forests of the Garo Hills, typically found near rocky streams at altitudes between 600 and 1,100 meters.
ai.behavior: Leptobrachella nokrekensis is primarily nocturnal, remaining active along rocky stream banks at night to forage for small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Leptobrachella nokrekensis* breeds during the monsoon (June–August), depositing small clutches of unpigmented eggs in flowing forest streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Leptobrachella nokrekensis* is endemic to the Nokrek Biosphere Reserve in the Garo Hills of Meghalaya, India, occurring at elevations between 600 and 1,100 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Leptobrachella nokrekensis* consists of a series of high-pitched, pulsed notes emitted by individuals residing near fast-flowing rocky streams.
